pain.title: The real pains of bookmark management
pain.subtitle: Your bookmarks are scattered everywhere — once lost, duplicated, or scrambled, they're hard to get back.

lost.title: Bookmarks silently disappear
lost.desc: Mistakes, browser crashes, sync failures — years of curated links gone in a flash.

crossBrowser.title: Browsers don't talk to each other
crossBrowser.desc: Chrome, Edge, and Firefox each keep their own set, and the same bookmarks never line up across them.

migration.title: One reorganization scrambles everything
migration.desc: Rename, move, or merge a folder and children often vanish or the hierarchy turns into a mess — fixing it is a nightmare.

history.title: Deletes resurrect and edits overwrite
history.desc: A bookmark you deleted on computer A comes back; two devices edit at once and one side silently overwrites the other.

mixed.title: Work and personal bookmarks collide
mixed.desc: Everything sits in one tree: work links and personal saves get tangled together, and splitting them apart means hand-sorting folders.

lock.title: Native sync locks you into a vendor cloud
lock.desc: Chrome and Edge native sync stores your bookmarks in plaintext in the browser vendor's cloud: switch browsers and it breaks, privacy is out of your hands, and browsers never talk to each other.

features.title: An engine built for real sync scenarios
features.subtitle: More than a cloud backup — intelligent sync that actually preserves your bookmark structure.

sync.title: True tree structure, hierarchy never breaks
sync.desc: Sync keeps the tree as-is instead of flattening it into path strings. Rename, move, or reorder folders and every child and level is preserved — no more "renamed a folder and its children vanished".

spaces.title: Isolated sync spaces — work vs. personal
spaces.desc: Each space is an independent bookmark tree, bindable to different browser profiles. Free 1 space / Plus 3 / Pro 10; switching spaces switches sync context.

devices.title: Devices at a glance, unbind anytime
devices.desc: Syncing browsers register as devices automatically — view, rename, or unbind them. Remove old devices whenever you like.

history.title: Precise deletes, they never come back
history.desc: Deletes propagate across devices via tombstones. A bookmark removed on device A will never resurrect on device B from stale data.

quota.title: Tiered by count, only for capacity
quota.desc: Start with 1,000 free, 10,000 on Plus, unlimited on Pro (capped at ~250,000). All tiers share identical sync features — upgrade purely for headroom.

privacy.title: Content encryption, your choice
privacy.desc: End-to-end encryption is on by default: every bookmark operation is encrypted on your device before upload, so the server only holds ciphertext — even BookmarkSync itself can't read your bookmarks. Keys never touch the server; on a new device, just sign in and enter the same passphrase — no 44-character key to remember.

conflict.title: Automatic merge, nothing overwritten
conflict.desc: Two devices editing, deleting, and adding at once are reconciled by intelligent three-way merge — both sides' additions survive, nothing is blindly overwritten or lost. Offline edits merge in the moment you reconnect.

migration.title: Free cross-account migration
migration.desc: Sign in to any account to pull the full bookmark tree. New devices and new accounts initialize in seconds — no HTML exports, no manual cleanup.

order.title: Order follows you — reorder once, everywhere
order.desc: Drag to reorder folders and bookmarks on one device, and every other device keeps the same order. The engine converges on fractional sort keys instead of scrambling your arrangement into an internal ID order — what you see is what stays.

browsers.title: Works with major browsers
browsers.subtitle: Install once — one setup unlocks all your bookmarks in the browsers you use daily.

upgrade.q: Do the tiers differ in features?
upgrade.a: No. All three tiers share identical features — true-tree sync (renaming/moving folders never loses items), precise deletion, multi-device auto-merge, and end-to-end encryption enabled by default. The only differences are capacity: bookmark count (Pro unlimited, capped at ~250,000), sync spaces (Free 1 / Plus 3 / Pro 10), and devices (Free 3 / Plus 6 / Pro 15).

refund.a: No-questions-asked refund within 7 days of your first subscription. Beyond that, refunds are available for serious technical issues. See Terms of Service Section 4 for details.

freeLimit.q: How many bookmarks does each tier hold?
freeLimit.a: Bookmarks: Free up to 1,000, Plus up to 10,000, Pro unlimited (capped at ~250,000). Sync spaces: Free 1, Plus 3, Pro 10. Devices: Free 3, Plus 6, Pro 15.

payment.q: What payment methods do you accept?
payment.a: Via Creem we support Visa / Mastercard / Alipay / WeChat Pay and other major channels.

subOrOnetime.q: Why a subscription instead of a one-time purchase?
subOrOnetime.a: Sync continuously consumes server and bandwidth resources. A subscription keeps revenue aligned with cost and lets us maintain the service long term. Plus is $20/yr and Pro is $50/yr, cancel anytime, and you keep access until the end of the current billing period.

order.q: Will sync scramble my bookmark and folder order?
order.a: No. Every bookmark carries a sort key and sync converges on it: reorder by dragging on one device, and the others follow. If two devices insert at the same spot concurrently, they still converge to one deterministic order (tie-broken by unique ID) — no overwrites, no random shuffling.

passphrase.q: What if I forget my sync passphrase?
passphrase.a: The passphrase is the only key to decrypt: losing it means the encrypted cloud data can never be decrypted. Save it in a password manager. New versions sync the salt in the cloud, so you only need the same passphrase on a new device — no manual key export.

newDevice.q: How do I restore bookmarks on a new device / after reinstall?

devices.a: Yes. Syncing browsers register as devices automatically; in the Spaces & Devices panel you can view, rename, or unbind them. Remove old devices whenever needed.

autoSync.q: Can I turn off automatic sync?
autoSync.a: Yes. Turn off the auto-sync toggle under Advanced in the options page; sync then only runs when you tap Sync Now.

gc.q: Does cloud log compaction delete my bookmarks?
gc.a: No. Compaction only merges historical operation records to save storage; it never deletes bookmarks. It runs automatically on the server as needed.

quotaUnit.q: Is the quota counted by bookmarks or bytes?
quotaUnit.a: Enforcement is by bytes (the only server-enforceable metric under E2EE): Free 5MB / Plus 20MB / Pro 500MB. Free and Plus are calibrated at ~2KB per bookmark with headroom (1,000 bookmarks → 5MB, 10,000 → 20MB); Pro is unlimited at 500MB ≈ a 250,000 cap. When over quota, new changes pause; delete bookmarks or spaces to free up space and sync resumes automatically. Already-synced data is unaffected.

privacy.title: Privacy Policy
privacy.intro: We take your privacy seriously. This policy explains how BookmarkSync collects, stores, and uses your data.

collect.title: What we collect
collect.body: Only the minimum data needed to run the service: email address (for sign-in), browser bookmarks (for sync). We also collect two things that **you provide or the extension attaches automatically, and that never contain bookmark content**: (1) feedback you submit in the extension plus an optional reply email; (2) diagnostic metadata reported automatically on sync errors (extension version, browser, UI language, failing stage and error type). We do not collect browsing history, do not track usage behavior, and do not embed third-party analytics.

store.title: How data is stored
store.body: Bookmark data is stored in Supabase (a PostgreSQL-based BaaS) with row-level security (RLS) enabled — each user can only read and write their own data. **End-to-end encryption is on by default**: every bookmark operation is encrypted on your device before upload, so the server only stores ciphertext — even a full database export reveals no bookmark content. The encryption key is derived from your passphrase (or exported and imported on a new device) and never touches the server. Login credentials are managed by Supabase Auth; we do not store plaintext passwords.

use.title: How data is used
use.body: Bookmark data is used solely for cross-browser sync. It will never be used for ads, marketing, user profiling, or any commercial analytics. Feedback and error diagnostics are used only to investigate issues, improve the product, and reply to you.

share.title: Do we share with third parties
share.body: No. We do not sell, rent, or trade any of your data. Payment is processed by Creem — we only receive payment success notifications, never your card details.

delete.title: How to delete data
delete.body: To delete your account and all cloud bookmark data, contact support{'@'}bookmark-sync.top — we process it within 7 days. Bookmarks on each device can be deleted directly in the browser; deletion syncs across devices as a tombstone.

contact.title: Contact us
contact.body: For any questions about this policy, contact support{'@'}bookmark-sync.top.

faq.title: FAQ
faq.subtitle: Common questions about sign-up, browser support, security and sync.

account.a: Yes. Register with email + password, set a sync passphrase after signing in, and start syncing bookmarks across browsers.

browsers.a: Chrome, Edge, and Firefox (Manifest V3). Safari is not supported yet.

free.q: Can I use the free plan?
free.a: Yes. The free plan syncs 1,000 bookmarks with no credit card, and all sync features are identical to paid plans.

restore.q: How do I restore bookmarks on a new device?
restore.a: Install the extension → sign in with the same account → enter the same sync passphrase, and your full bookmark tree is pulled automatically.

security.a: Yes. End-to-end encryption (AES-256-GCM) is enforced by default: every operation is encrypted on your device before upload, the server stores only ciphertext, and no third party — including us — can read your bookmarks.

passphrase.q: What if I forget my sync passphrase?
passphrase.a: The passphrase is stored only on your device and never uploaded; it is the only key to decrypt cloud bookmarks. It cannot be changed once set — if forgotten, your bookmarks cannot be decrypted. Keep it safe.

conflict.q: What happens when multiple devices edit at the same time?
conflict.a: No. Concurrent changes are merged automatically with all additions kept; deletes propagate as tombstones, so removed bookmarks never resurrect from stale data.

gc.q: Is cloud data cleaned up automatically?
gc.a: Yes. Server-managed GC automatically compacts stale operation logs with a dynamic threshold — no manual setup needed.

accountBar.q: Why is there an extra "Account Bookmarks Bar" folder under Other Bookmarks in Firefox / Edge?
accountBar.a: When Chrome is signed into a Google account, it has a separate "account bookmarks bar" distinct from your local bar. Firefox and Edge have no native place for it, so the extension collects those bookmarks into a same-named "Account Bookmarks Bar" folder under Other Bookmarks, so you can still see and edit them there. This is by design—not a duplicate and not a bug. The bookmarks inside match exactly what you see in Chrome, and editing on any device syncs everywhere. On Firefox / Edge it stays as a folder permanently; it works the same.
